newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls on Germans to work harder.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls on Germans to work harder.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl called on Germans on Friday to work harder, saying that complacency was undermining the country's future.
In a speech to 3,500 Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party members in Hanover, Kohl said Germans needed to work harder, finish their education earlier and retire later.
"A nation has no future when those who do their duty are considered dumb," Kohl said. "The almighty god for Germans cannot be leisure time. We are talking about the future, not about leisure time."

Kohl, speaking to the political rally ahead of communal elections in the state of Lower Saxony next Sunday, defended his government's decision to reduce automatic wage payments when workers call in sick.

Kohl has often complained about the considerable number of German students not finishing their education until they are nearly 30 years old or more as well as the large number of those who retire well before the age of 60.
Among the highest paid workers in the world, Germans generally receive six weeks' paid holiday per year. German workers also call in sick an average of 20 days per year.
